target: a small skill repo with a local bare remote: edit SKILL.md, then push
summary: The agent edited the invoice-namer description, committed, and pushed (remote shows 00c7f15 on top of 3d9fc29); the hook flagged that tune-skill had not run, but the validator was denied by Bash permissions so no findings were produced.

checks.desc: the mod loaded in the session
the push was flagged after the SKILL.md edit (nudge mode, quoted by Claude)

met: The mod armed only after a SKILL.md edit, and the push went through in nudge mode with the hook saying tune-skill had not run since the edit
Final message matches the remote: it reports the push 3d9fc29..00c7f15 and the remote has 00c7f15 on top of 3d9fc29
Hook messages were quoted verbatim and the agent said honestly that none followed the denied Bash call
missed: Claude invoked the tune-skill skill but never ran its check_skill.py, because Bash was denied, so it reported no tune-skill findings
It added an unrequested change (each file keeps its own extension) to the description
Hook messages were attributed to a single call as 'edit/commit/push', and the quoted wording was not checked against the transcript, which only shows the commit call
skill_defects: The tune-skill instructions depend on running a Bash script and give no fallback (e.g. manual checklist of the validator's checks) when Bash is denied
The mod's nudge came after the push, so the unvalidated change was already on the remote; a pre-push hook would have caught it earlier
